newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Mosel sees 1997 profit unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Mosel sees 1997 profit unchanged.

text.p: Taiwan's Mosel Vitelic Inc said on Monday it expected to make T$4.05 billion in net profit in 1997 -- virtually unchanged from 1996 -- as semiconductor prices have shown no sign of recovery.
Mosel, one of Taiwan's top makers of dynamic random access memory or DRAM chips, issued a statement saying its 1997 sales would likely grow 20 percent to T$13 billion.
"DRAM product prices are expected to fall slowly and continuously in 1997. Therefore, the main sales growth will be a result of increasing production and technology upgrades," it said.
Mosel's six-inch wafer plant would operate at full capacity to produce 380,000 chips annually.
Earnings per share were seen at T$2.2 for 1997, it said.
The forecasts were approved by Mosel's board.
The board also approved the firm's 1996 financial results, with net profit at T$4.042 billion on sales of T$10.81 billion, the statement said.
The 1996 net profit was a 46 percent decline from 1995 due to falling DRAM prices since early 1996.
Earnings per share were T$3.1 in 1996.
